meta.title: Year 7 – Secondary School Start | DigiOpo
meta.description: DigiOpo – Year 7 student counselling. Secondary school start – discover your strengths and learn study skills.

hero.intro: A new chapter begins – and it's exciting! In secondary school you develop study skills, discover your own strengths and start thinking about your future.

timetable.heading: Your timetable changes – new subjects ahead
timetable.intro: Moving to secondary school brings new subjects to your timetable. The primary school subject 'Environmental Studies' splits into five separate subjects in Year 7: biology, geography, physics, chemistry and health education.

johdanto.heading: Welcome to secondary school
johdanto.subtitle: First lesson: orientation and survival guide
johdanto.p1: In secondary school you develop study skills, discover your own strengths and start thinking about your future.
johdanto.p2: Everything feels a little new at the start – and that's completely normal.
johdanto.p3: You're not alone – everyone else is in the same situation.

robo_bubble: Psst. I also started from scratch once. Here's the guide that helped. 👇

selviytymisopas.heading: Secondary School Survival Guide
selviytymisopas.subtitle: Four ways to survive everyday secondary school life

robo_tarina.heading: Robo arrives at secondary school
robo_tarina.desc: Get to know Robo and AI – and write a letter to yourself in the future. What do you dream of? What are you afraid of? What do you want to remember?

mission_tervetuloa.heading: Operation Secondary School
mission_tervetuloa.intro: You will do this task in groups. The teacher gives each group an envelope – inside are four checkpoint cards. Solve the checkpoints in order, moving together.
mission_tervetuloa.li1: Open Checkpoint 1 and read the instructions aloud together
mission_tervetuloa.li2: Solve the task – the group decides when it's ready
mission_tervetuloa.li3: Only then open the next card
mission_tervetuloa.li4: At the last checkpoint you prepare a presentation for the whole class

teacher_material.open_link: Open teacher guide and problem cards
teacher_material.desc_tervetuloa: Contains teacher instructions, group passport (print one per group) and laminate checkpoint cards 1–6.
teacher_material.desc_motivaatio: Contains teacher instructions with steps and 6 printable problem cards (one per group). Open in browser and print.
teacher_material.desc_vahvuushuutokauppa: Contains teacher instructions and 4 printable group cards – each with all 15 strengths with checkboxes and point entry fields. Open in browser and print.
teacher_material.desc_tulevaisuus: Contains teacher instructions for the Future task: goals, timing, differentiation tips and debriefing and assessment questions.

challenge.summary_toggle: Summary – what I learned in this lesson
challenge.johdanto_ohje: Write a letter to yourself three years from now: What do you hope to be? What are you afraid of? What is there in you now that you do not want to forget? Keep the letter and read it in 9th grade.
challenge.johdanto_vihje: 💡 Tip: Write honestly — the letter is just for you
challenge.opiskelutaidot_ohje: Create a personal study plan for yourself: choose one subject you want to focus on this week. Write down when you will study, how, and how you will assess your success at the end of the week.
challenge.opiskelutaidot_vihje: 💡 Tip: Small, concrete goals work better than big dreams
challenge.motivaatio_ohje: Keep a motivation diary for a week: write down one thing each day that inspired you to learn — and note whether it was internal (I wanted to) or external (I had to / expected). Reflect at the end of the week: which gives you more energy?
challenge.motivaatio_vihje: 💡 Tip: Even small things count — like that one lesson when time flew by
challenge.vahvuudet_ohje: Create your own strength map: write on paper all the things you think you are good at — even the ones that seem small. Categorize the strengths: social, creative, technical, physical. Which category is your strongest?
challenge.vahvuudet_vihje: 💡 Tip: Ask someone who knows you well to add one strength to the list that you did not notice yourself
challenge.summary_ohje: This lesson you practised imagining the future – the most important skill in a changing world.
challenge.summary_li1: 🚀 I completed the Time Travel to the Future task with Robo
challenge.summary_li2: 💭 I practised imagining what kind of adult I could become
challenge.summary_li3: 💼 I thought about what kind of work I would like to try by 2045
challenge.summary_li4: ⭐ I wrote down one dream and one concrete step
challenge.summary_li5: 🤔 I practised the most important skill: what do I do when I do not know what to do?
challenge.summary_vihje: 💡 Remember: daydreaming is not laziness – it is a skill you can practise!

opiskelutaidot.badge: Survival skill 1 – learn how to learn!
opiskelutaidot.heading: Learn, grow, shine
opiskelutaidot.p1: Everyone learns differently. Some learn by listening, others by doing. A good learner tries different approaches, doesn't give up immediately and asks for help.
opiskelutaidot.p2: Learning is not a gift – it's a skill.
opiskelutaidot.tasks_desc: Four tasks where you practise the most important learning skills.
opiskelutaidot.card4_desc: Try a new way of learning!

pakopeli.heading: Secondary school escape game: learn how to learn!
pakopeli.desc: Can you escape? Solve the tasks and discover your own learning styles by playing.

tiedon_temppeli.heading: 🏛️ Temple of Knowledge
tiedon_temppeli.desc: Can you reach the top of the temple? Speed is everything!

motivaatio.heading: Get inspired again
motivaatio.question: What gets you moving?
motivaatio.subtitle: Motivation can come from two directions – and both work.
motivaatio.inner_heading: I do it because I want to
motivaatio.inner_desc: You get energy from the doing or learning itself.
motivaatio.outer_heading: I do it because I have to or get a reward
motivaatio.outer_desc: Energy comes from outside: a grade, praise or consequences.
motivaatio.q1: Is there a subject that feels easy for you? Why?
motivaatio.q2: Is there a subject you only do because you have to? How does that feel?
motivaatio.q3: What would happen if grades were removed completely?

kadonnut_motivaatio.heading: Lost motivation
kadonnut_motivaatio.desc: Motivation has gone missing – can you find it? Play and discover your own ways to keep going.

motivaatiotori.heading: Motivation Market
motivaatiotori.intro: Each group is given one motivation problem card. First the group comes up with its own solutions, then you go around improving each other's ideas.
motivaatiotori.li1: Read your card's problem aloud to the group
motivaatiotori.li2: Write down all solution ideas on the card (3 min)
motivaatiotori.li3: Move to the next card — add or improve ideas (3 min/round)
motivaatiotori.li4: Return to your own card and choose the best idea
motivaatiotori.li5: Present the problem and winning idea to the class (30 sec)
motivaatiotori.hint: ⏱ Time: 20–25 min · Group size: 3–4 students · Moving

vahvuudet.heading: Know yourself, trust yourself
vahvuudet.p1: Everyone has strengths. When you know yourself, you make better choices.

supervoimat.heading: Superpowers – discover your own strengths!
supervoimat.desc: Play an interactive story and find out what your superpowers are. Make choices and discover yourself!

vahvuushuutokauppa.heading: Strength Auction
vahvuushuutokauppa.intro: Each group is given a budget: 10 points and a list of 15 strengths. The group decides together which 3 strengths it wants to "buy" — and why those ones.
vahvuushuutokauppa.hint: ⏱ Time: 20–25 min · Group size: 3–4 students · Moving

tulevaisuus.heading: Dream, explore, grow
tulevaisuus.p1: You can't know the future in advance — but you can practise imagining it. Dreaming is not laziness. It's a skill needed when the world changes and familiar tools disappear.
tulevaisuus.open_in_tab: 🔗 Open task in its own tab (if the view is cramped)
tulevaisuus.p2: In this lesson you do the Time Travel to the Future task: you travel with Robo to the year 2045, make choices and write about your dreams. At the same time you practise the most important skill: what do I do when I don't know what to do?

teppo.heading: TEPPO – Work-oriented basic education
teppo.subtitle: TEPPO makes working life familiar already in school!
teppo.p1: TEPPO is flexible work-oriented basic education for Years 8–9. Studies alternate between work placement periods at workplaces and teaching at school.
teppo.p2: Applications open in spring January–March – open to all Year 7 and 8 students.
teppo.fact2_desc: 5–7 weeks a year at real workplaces.
teppo.fact3_desc: January–March through Wilma or paper form.
teppo.fact4_desc: Regardless of whether you're aiming for upper secondary or vocational school.
teppo.cta: 💼 Ask your school counsellor about TEPPO – applications open in January!

koulun_jalkeen.heading: After school
koulun_jalkeen.subtitle: Find meaningful activities for your free time.
koulun_jalkeen.p1: School is just part of the day. In your free time you learn things that aren't taught at school — and you might find something that becomes important to you.

structure: Intro: New subjects in lower secondary school – the timetable changes (5 min)
What is student counselling? – infographic and short introduction (5 min)
The lower secondary survival guide – what four skills do you need? (5 min)
Interactive story: Robo arrives at lower secondary school (20–25 min)
Operation Upper School – group task on a station trail (20–25 min)
objectives: You know what new subjects are waiting in 7th grade
You know what student counselling is and who to ask for help
You know what four survival skills you need in lower secondary school
You recognise that feeling nervous in a new situation is normal
You have met Robo and written some thoughts to yourself about the future
summary: You know what new subjects there are in 7th grade
You can name the four skills in the Lower Secondary Survival Guide
You know what student counselling means and who your counsellor is
You have written a letter to yourself – your thoughts saved for the future
You can name at least three adults at school you can ask for help
johdanto.why: The transition from primary to secondary school is one of the most sensitive phases in a student's educational journey: a good start strengthens engagement with school, which predicts both learning outcomes and wellbeing throughout the secondary years. Getting to know the new subjects and student counselling right from the start gives pupils an overview of secondary school — and the four survival skills provide a concrete framework for the whole of secondary school.

structure: Intro: how do you learn best? (5 min)
Escape game: learn how to learn (20 min)
Task stations: memory, reading, schedules, AI (your choice)
Wrap-up: one new technique to try this week (5 min)
objectives: You understand how the brain learns: repetition, sleep, and breaks are part of learning
You try at least one new study technique
You understand that learning is a skill that can be practised — not a gift you are born with
summary: You can explain why cramming the night before a test does not work
You know at least two techniques that help things stick in your memory
You have a plan for how to try a new technique before the next test
opiskelutaidot.why: Research shows that the most effective study techniques — such as self-testing and spaced repetition — are precisely the ones students use least. Learning these techniques now will save you hundreds of hours of work during secondary school, exams, and later further studies.

structure: Intro: when did you last get excited about something? (5 min)
Discussion: where does motivation come from and where does it go? (10 min)
objectives: You know that motivation is not a fixed trait but a state you can influence
You recognise things that drain or fuel your own enthusiasm
You learn to tell the difference between inner drive and external pressure
summary: You can name three things that affect your own motivation
You know at least one way to get yourself moving on a boring day
You understand the difference: I do it because I want to vs. I do it because I have to
mina-oppijana.why: Motivation research shows that enthusiasm comes from three things: making your own decisions, learning and succeeding, and belonging to a group. When you recognise these, you stop waiting for motivation to 'come back on its own' — and you learn to seek it actively. You will need this skill every time a boring patch hits at school, in a hobby, or later at work.

structure: Intro: what are you good at — even outside school? (5 min)
Activity: Superpowers — find your own strengths (20 min)
Pair discussion: what strength does your friend see in you? (10 min)
objectives: You identify at least three of your own character strengths
You understand that strengths are more than just school subjects
You practise describing yourself positively
summary: You can name your core strengths and give an example of each
You know that strengths can be developed by using them
You have practised saying something good about yourself out loud
omat-vahvuudet.why: Research shows that recognising and using your own strengths is linked to wellbeing and school success. In practice you will need this skill soon: when applying for a work placement, thinking about upper secondary options, and in every situation where you need to say who you are and what you can do.

objectives: You review content from different subjects through a game
You notice which topic areas are strong for you and which need more revision
You experience that recalling information from memory is effective practice
summary: You have reviewed content from several subjects by playing
You know which topics went well and what is worth revising
You have experienced how retrieval practice teaches
tiedon-temppeli.why: A quiz is not just fun — it is proven to be one of the most effective ways to learn. When you have to retrieve an answer from memory, the memory trace strengthens far more than from simply reading. This is called the testing effect.

structure: Intro: what would you like to try sometime? (5 min)
Time travel to the future task: a journey with Robo to 2045, choices and your own dreams (10–15 min)
Debrief: sharing dreams — what came up for many? (10 min)
objectives: You practise imagining different futures
You notice that dreaming and coming up with ideas are skills, not laziness
You learn to act in a situation where there is no ready-made right answer
summary: You have imagined your own future and written down one dream
You can tolerate a situation where there is no right answer
You know that you can shape the future with your own choices — one small step at a time
tulevaisuus.why: Futures researchers talk about futures literacy: the ability to imagine multiple possible futures and act even when you do not know for certain what will happen. Many jobs you will do as an adult do not exist yet — which is why the ability to imagine is just as important a skill as reading or arithmetic.

objectives: You know what TEPPO — the work-oriented basic education programme — is
You know who it is suitable for and how to apply
You can assess whether TEPPO might be the right path for you
summary: You know the basics of TEPPO: who, what, and when to apply
You can explain to a guardian what TEPPO is about
You know who to ask for more information if you are interested
teppo.why: Some people learn best by doing. TEPPO is an official way to complete basic education in which workplace learning and school alternate. It is worth knowing about this already in 7th grade, because applications open in spring — and the decision affects your everyday life.
